as_told.title: Eric Hecker's South Pole neutrino emitters claim

plain: IceCube, a large detector buried in the ice of Antarctica that catches tiny particles called neutrinos, is said by some to be a two-way machine that can also send energy out, even as a kind of earthquake weapon, with a link drawn to Christchurch, New Zealand. A researcher named Jay Anderson relays this as the claim of a man named Eric Hecker, saying Hecker has found documents that "insinuate it's a two-way device" able to emit energy. Michels tells it directly as Hecker's claim that there are neutrino detectors and emitters at the South Pole. If true, it would mean a science station hides a weapon.
